title: Crochet notions and accessories
subtitle: What you actually need and what is optional
excerpt: Beyond hook and yarn, a handful of small tools make crochet more accurate and more comfortable. Most are cheap and reusable across years of projects. This is what to get and why.
sourceNotes: Pauline Turner, How to Crochet — tools and equipment. Edie Eckman, The Crochet Answer Book.

glossaryTerms.definition: A blunt-tipped large-eye sewing needle used to weave in yarn tails and seam crochet pieces. Also called a yarn needle or darning needle. The blunt tip is essential — a sharp needle splits the yarn rather than passing through it.
A small mechanical or digital counter that clicks forward one number with each press. Used to track the current row number in long projects where losing count would mean frogging back to check.

heroPrompt: A flat lay of crochet notions on a pale linen surface: a 4 mm aluminium hook, a ball of cream DK cotton, four locking stitch markers, a tapestry needle, small scissors, a soft tape measure, and a row counter.

content.text: The essential kit for a beginner crocheter is short: a hook, yarn, a
, and scissors. Everything else is useful but not required for the first few projects.
Crochet hook: the size specified by the pattern, or a 4 mm hook for a first DK project.
Yarn: the weight the pattern calls for. Plain cotton or smooth DK for a first project.
Tapestry needle: for weaving in tails. Buy a pack of 4-6 — they are cheap and easy to lose.
Small scissors: a dedicated pair that lives in the project bag.
Stitch markers (locking type): 6-10 is enough for most projects. Useful from the first round project.
Soft tape measure: for checking gauge and finished measurements.
earns its place on blankets, garments, and any project with more than 40 rows.
Blocking mat and pins: needed once you start blocking pieces. A pack of foam interlocking tiles works; dedicated blocking boards are also available.
A hook roll or project bag: keeps the tools together when the project is put down mid-row.

attrs.title: What not to buy yet
attrs.body: A full hook set in every size from 0.6 mm to 25 mm. Buy the size you need, then the next two sizes either side. A complete set is a vanity purchase for a beginner — most of the sizes will gather dust for years.
